title: How US' Somnigroup's Q2 net income rose 12% despite sales decline?
content:
Somnigroup’s Q2 FY26 net income rose 12 per cent to $110.9 million despite a 3 per cent sales decline to $1.82 billion, supported by margin expansion and higher operating income. 
Gross margin improved to 44.8 per cent, while EBITDA rose to $280.8 million. 
The company raised 2026 EPS guidance and focuses on Mattress Firm integration, the Stearns & Foster launch and Leggett & Platt acquisition.

title: Pakistan's textile surge signals a South Asian sourcing shift
content:
Pakistan's textile exports hit a record $1.83 billion in July 2026, up 9 per cent year-on-year after a flat FY2025-26.
Bangladesh's gas-constrained garment factories running at 60–70 per cent capacity are pushing buyers to reassess South Asian cotton-heavy sourcing.
With no US tariff edge and a widening deficit, August data, LNG supply and rupee stability will decide if allocations scale.

title: EXIM Bank replaces RBI as India's export subsidy implementing agency
content:
India has shifted implementation of the Interest Subvention Support Scheme for pre- and post-shipment export credit under the Export Promotion Mission from the Reserve Bank of India to EXIM Bank, effective April 1, 2026. 
EXIM Bank will manage operations, verification and claim settlements, while the RBI will continue processing supplementary claims for the January-March 2026 quarter.

title: PM Modi honours weavers, artisans on National Handloom Day
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi greeted the citizens of India on National Handloom Day and celebrated the country's handloom heritage.
He paid tribute to weavers and artisans for preserving traditional craft skills across generations.
The government will continue supporting handlooms as a pillar of rural empowerment, women-led development and Atmanirbhar Bharat.

title: South India's cotton yarn stable, faces higher cost but slower demand
content:
Cotton yarn prices held steady in Mumbai and Tiruppur after mills passed higher cotton costs to buyers. 
Mumbai saw subdued grey and finished fabric demand at higher levels, while Tiruppur reported stronger weaving ahead of the festive season. 
Gujarat cotton rose on firmer ICE futures, a higher Cotton Corporation of India auction base and scarce quality fibre, lifting costs for southern mills.

title: US cotton rewrites Bangladesh's apparel sourcing playbook
content:
Bangladesh Bank has raised the cash incentive for exporters using local yarn and fabric to 5 per cent in FY27, from 1.5 per cent.
A draft import policy lifts value addition to 30 per cent for most clothing, with incentives and duty-free inputs at stake.
US zero-tariff volumes depend on US cotton and man-made fibre use, while 16.5 per cent base duty and a 10 per cent forced-labour tariff remain.
